Volkswagen ID. Every1 Virtually Morphs Into the ID. Up! and the GTI Version Also Comes Forward
9 photos
Photo: kdesignag / Instagram
Volkswagen AG launched the ID. series more than half a decade ago as their next-generation family of battery, plug-in hybrid, and extended-range electric cars primarily using the dedicated MEB all-electric platform.
The namesake Volkswagen brand introduced the series as its first purpose-built electric vehicle family with the ID.3 hatchback, and the family has grown to include a multitude of vehicles of all shapes and sizes, both offered into series production and as concept cars. There are even models that have already left their life – like the ID4. and ID.5 crossover SUVs. That’s because Volkswagen is welcoming a new age for the series, where the numbers are replaced with more common denominators – like the ID. Polo and ID. Polo GTI, the newly launched ID. Cross, as well as the larger ID. Tiguan .
The series has grown extremely vast, by the way, as the models that are sold in Europe or North America are also joined by a variety of China-focused nameplates that will probably never reach the Old Continent or American shores. Anyway, with all the commotion going on, it’s no wonder the rumor mill keeps a close eye on them.
According to the latest reports, the next introductions for the ID. series could be the Volkswagen ID. Up! or Lupo, set to become the tiniest member of the family, as well as another China-dedicated model. Now, the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI have also joined the chat, this time around focusing on the potential Volkswagen ID. Up!
More precisely, Kleber Silva, a Brazil-based virtual artist known as " KDesign AG " on social media, has decided to have a CGI go at imagining the return of the small VW passenger car as a direct follow-up to the A-segment Volkswagen ID. Every1 hatchback concept, introduced for the first time during the spring season of 2025 and expected to enter production sometime in 2027.
This could become both the smallest and most affordable Volkswagen in the ID. series, and the company might choose to give it a known name like the Up! or Lupo to keep in line with the new nameplate strategy. The pixel master has gone with the Volkswagen ID. Up! nameplate for this unofficial, hypothetical design project, by the way, and we don’t mind.
The CGI expert kept everything simple and on point – hearing the speculation regarding the name of the new tiny EV , they imagined how the production version of this ultra-compact model could look based on the Every1 concept. Even better, the author also cooked up a GTI version to join the real world’s ID. Polo GTI at a lower price point. So, what do you think – yay or nay?
